  * The EU’s ‘strategic partnership’ with Azerbaijan, and any other authoritarian regimes committing similar abuses, is in direct violation of Article 21 TEU.  
    * It is not sustainable for the EU to, once crises arise, transfer (energy) dependencies from one dictator onto the next.

    * Authoritarian leaders are unreliable. They do not make trustworthy partners. Energy deals legitimize them, financially contribute to human rights abuses, and make the Union vulnerable to extortion while restricting political manoeuvrability.

    * The EU should avoid indulging in new strategic partnerships with authoritarian regimes and should end any such cooperation already in existence.  
    * The EU’s energy policy should be guided by the concept of friend shoring, which entails the focusing of supply chains on countries regarded as political and economic allies, or at least those not seen to be in direct violation of our fundamental principles.

## **Noting that:**

* The European Parliament on October 4, 2023, adopted a resolution (2023/2879(RSP)) calling on the EU to reduce dependency on gas exports from Azerbaijan but to suspend all imports only “in the event of military aggression against Armenian territorial integrity or significant hybrid attacks against Armenia’s constitutional order and democratic institutions”.

## **Calls upon:**

* The EU to keep assessing sources of imports of oil and gas other than from Azerbaijan and work on arranging them as soon as possible;  
  * The European Commission not to enter into new strategic partnerships with authoritarian regimes without the explicit approval of the European Parliament.

  63. ##  **Resolution on strengthening liberal democracy in the Republic of Moldova and the Eastern Partnership**

Submitted by: USR Tineret, JOVD, CUB Junior

Co-signers: VU, Mladé ANO, JNC, Attīstībai Youth, ERPY, LHG, LLY, Momentum TizenX, Ógra Fianna Fáil, Junge Liberale, ZeMolodizhka, European Youth of Ukraine (Ukraine), Young Progressives (MPS), LUF, FEL, CUF, Unge Venstre,

Adopted at the Autumn Congress 2023 in Riga, Latvia on 11 November 2023\.

## **Considering that:**

* Considering the crucial importance of upholding and promoting liberal democratic values in Europe;

  * Recognizing the challenges faced by the Republic of Moldova in its journey towards political stability, economic prosperity, and European Union integration;

    * Acknowledging the potential of the Republic of Moldova to serve as a model for liberal democracy in the Eastern Partnership region;  
    * Emphasizing the need for active engagement and support from LYMEC and its member organizations to support liberal values and reforms in Moldova and the Eastern partnership;

## **Recognizing that:**

the Republic of Moldova shares the values of the European Union;

* the EU’s role was very important from the initial stage as the Republic has been guided and monitored by the EU since the partnership and Cooperation Agreement came into effect in 1998;

* the Association Agreement that was signed between the EU and the Republic of Moldova on the 27th June 2014 established a new judicial framework for the advancement of the relations between Republic of Moldova and EU to a new level of political association and economic integration between the EU and Eastern Europe;  
  * the Republic of Moldova has taken considerable steps to become a solid, stable and prosperous part of the EU's neighborhood in the past years through various reform processes;  
    * the Russian Federation continues to exert pressure on the Moldovan authorities and citizens by keeping “peacekeeper” soldiers on its Eastern occupied territory (region of Transnistria);

    * the Russian Federation brutally and illegally started a war of aggression in Ukraine, permanently disrupting the balance in Europe,

## **Believing that:**

* it is essential to have a democratic and amicable relationship as well as for having long-standing prosperity and stability at the borders of the EU;  
  * the citizens of the Republic of Moldova have a right to live a prosperous life in accordance to their desire to join the European Union;  
    * this is the beginning of a new period, which requires considerable efforts directed to the achievement of the objective of integration into the EU;

    * there should be zero tolerance for the Russian Federation’s aggression that has continuously tried to sabotage the Republic of Moldova’s path towards becoming a consolidated, European democracy;  
    * it is vitally important to educate young people in the Republic of Moldova and its Eastern occupied territory (region of Transnistria) about their shared past and to improve communication between both sides through broad social projects to benefit future reintegration and educational opportunities such as the Erasmus+ program.

## **LYMEC calls on the Republic of Moldova to:**

●

continue being invested in achieving statal reforms needed to comply with the Copenhagen criteria and to be focused on helping public institutions, citizens and the business community to benefit from the opportunities;

* continue investment in peaceful and diplomatic ways of reaching a resolution to the Transnistrian conflict;  
  * improve the knowledge and understanding of Moldovan citizens about the European path of the Republic of Moldova and to articulate that accession to the European community is not only the responsibility of the government, but also of the society itself.

## **LYMEC calls on the European Union to:**

* treat the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine candidate status to join the Union with the utmost importance and offer them the possibility of gradual rapprochement to the European family while bolstering European aspirations of Georgian people but not tolerating the pro-Russian course of the current Georgian authorities, so that impose sanctions on local officials who help to evade actual regime of sanctions, imposed on Russia;  
  * be committed towards finding the best solutions to support the

  Chisinau government to overcome threats posed by the Russian Federation via disinformation, economic pressures or any other type of malevolent action;

    * support the Republic of Moldova's set path towards energy independence, and help them build sustainable sources of energy;  
    * provide a straightforward approach to the EU and the Republic of Moldova when it comes to international trade. In order to bring the Republic Moldova closer to the European Union, the EU should gradually eliminate as many taxes of the trade between them in order to facilitate the integration through market forces;  
    * to ensure the fact that the process of European integration is not only a process of collaboration with the government, but with all relevant political and civic forces.

## **LYMEC calls on its MOs to:**

* raise awareness in their organizations about the need to expand the EU with other states, such as the ones in the Eastern Partnership and the Balkans; continue lobbying their mother-parties and governments for financial and logistical resources to help the Eastern Partnership countries realize reforms and break loose from the Russian Federation;  
  * organize study visits and on-the ground events that will help to better understanding the region.

64. ##  **The European Union Needs a Single Sanctions Coordinator**

Submitted by: Lithuanian Liberal Youth (LLY), Momentum TizenX, Unge Venstre (NUV), Nowoczesna Youth, Ógra Fianna Fáil, Young Liberals, Youth Movement for Rights and Freedoms (YMRF), Fédération des Etudiants Libéraux (FEL), Jongeren Organisatie Vrijheid en Democratie (JOVD), Jóvenes Ciudadanos (JC), Bundesverband Liberaler Hochschulgruppen (LHG), Jonk Demokraten (JDL), Svensk Ungdom (SU), Liberala

ungdomsförbundet (LUF), Centerstudenter, IMS Delegates, Jonge Democraten (JD), Jong

VLD, Centre Party Youth, Venstres Ungdom (VU), Joventut Nacionalista de Catalunya (JNC), European Youth of Ukraine (EYU), USR Tineret, Young Progressives (MPS), Attīstībai Youth (AY), Radikale Ungdom (RU), Mladé ANO, Junge Liberale (JuLis), ZeMolodizhka , Young Greenliberals Switzerland (YGL)

Adopted at the Autumn Congress 2023 in Riga, Latvia on 11 November 2023\.

## **Considering that:**

* Sanctions play a major role in response to terrorism, nuclear proliferation, military conflicts, and other foreign policy crises;

  * The European Union (EU) sanctions regime is managed by different bodies and actors, including the European Council, the European Commission, the European External Action Service (EEAS), and national governments. The multiplicity of actors can often lead to fragmentation, inconsistency, and confusion in the implementation and enforcement of sanctions across the EU;  
    * Despite the adoption of sanctions at the EU level, the lack of sanctions coordination in the bloc due to disjointed action by national authorities and differing judicial practices has resulted in inconsistent and unequal enforcement of sanctions by individual Member States;  
    * The lack of legal framework governing cooperation between the EU and major partners like the United States (US) hinders the effectiveness and transparency of the sanction process: informal cooperation behind closed doors is not sufficient to ensure a coordinated and effective approach on sanctions;  
    * The ongoing Russian war against Ukraine has highlighted the need for the EU to have a single sanctions coordinator, as the current system has proven to be ineffective: despite numerous rounds of sanctions imposed by the EU on Russia in the form of sanction packages, the process has been slow and the impact of these sanctions has been limited.

    * ​

## **Whereas:**

* Currently the Member States of the EU still continue trading with Russia by bypassing already imposed sanctions even with the new sanctions on Russia being implemented due to the ongoing war in Ukraine. Officials identified the UAE, Turkey, Armenia, Georgia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan as potential circumvention routes;  
  * The inconsistent enforcement of EU sanctions by individual Member States can lead to uneven consequences for those targeted by the sanctions: e.g., in 2017, the European Court of Justice ruled that Hungary had not properly enforced EU sanctions against Iran and that Hungary's failure to freeze the assets of an Iranian bank constituted a breach of EU law;  
    * The lack of cooperation between the EU and its partners creates difficulties for businesses operating across multiple Member States: e.g., in 2018, the French oil company “Total” was forced to withdraw from a major gas project in Iran after the US withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal and re-imposed sanctions. However, the withdrawal of “Total” was complicated by the fact that it was also subject to EU sanctions, which meant that it had to navigate differing enforcement regimes in individual Member States to comply with the sanctions;  
    * The lack of unified sanctions coordination undermines the ability to leverage political pressure against specific entities effectively: e.g., in 2019, it was reported that Italy had been blocking EU sanctions against Russia, citing concerns about the impact on Italian businesses. This illustrates the influence of political considerations in individual Member States on the enforcement of EU sanctions, which can undermine the unity and effectiveness of EU sanctions policy;  
    * Insufficient cooperation also leads to the fragmentation of the EU sanctions regime. Some EU Member States hesitated to enforce EU sanctions

against Russia over its occupation of Crimea and a full-scale invasion of Ukraine due to concerns about the impact on their own economies. This created a fragmentation of the EU sanctions regime, with different Member States enforcing the sanctions differently and potentially even adopting conflicting policies.

## **Recalling that:**

* The European Parliament's resolution of 13 March 2019 on the implementation of common foreign and security policy (annual report (2018/2157(INI)) contains a crucial section addressing the need for a single EU sanctions coordinator. This document highlights the urgent need for a more streamlined and coherent approach to the sanctions policy of the EU, which would be facilitated by appointing a dedicated coordinator to oversee and manage the implementation of sanctions across all EU Member States.

## **Believing that:**

* With the EU rapidly expanding the breadth and depth of its sanctions, it has

  become increasingly necessary to establish a unified system for their implementation, monitoring, and enforcement. This would ensure a more consistent

  and effective approach to sanctions, reducing the risk of violations and creating a more level playing field for economic actors;

  * Sanction efforts are most effective when coordinated and implemented

  multilaterally with allies, and poor design and implementation of sanctions policies often lead to them falling short of the desired effects.

## **Noting that:**

* Sanctions can take a variety of forms, such as trade restrictions, asset freezes, or travel bans, and they can be targeted at individuals, companies, or entire countries. Given the complexity of the external relations of the EU and the diversity of its Member States' foreign policy priorities, having a centralized authority to coordinate and harmonize sanctions policies could help ensure that the actions of the EU are more effective, coherent, consistent and transparent.

## **Calls upon:**

* The establishment of a single EU sanctions coordinator would streamline the process of implementing sanctions against countries or entities that violate international law or human rights. The coordinator would be responsible for

coordinating the efforts of various legal structures, ensuring that the sanctions are consistent with the foreign and security policy goals of the

EU, and taking into account the needs and capabilities of individual EU Member States;

* The EU to establish a structure or mechanism similar to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in the US, but specific to the EU, with the purpose of more effectively and efficiently managing sanctions and ensuring consistent enforcement across EU Member States. This structure or mechanism should work in tandem with the single EU sanctions coordinator and other relevant EU bodies as well as partners and should include provisions for regular reviews and updates to ensure that the sanctions policy remains effective and targeted;  
  * The EU to adopt a flexible and adaptive approach to sanctions policy, which would include regular reviews and updates to ensure that it remains effective and targeted in the context of a constantly evolving political and geopolitical landscape;

    * The EU and its Member States to adopt a transparent approach to sanctions policy, by providing regular updates and reports on the implementation and effectiveness of sanctions;  
    * The EU to establish a communication mechanism with the EEA and EFTA states to coordinate their joining of the sanctions’ regime and devise a harmonisation scheme to make sure the sanctions imposed reach their target;  
    * The EU to collaborate with other regional international and intergovernmental international organizations, such as the United Nations, to strengthen the effectiveness of sanctions and promote respect for human rights and international law.

  65. ##  **Ban Imports from Chinese Regions and Market Sectors Tainted by Forced Labour**

Mover: LUF

Co-signed by: ERPY, Unge Venstre, Venstres Ungdom, Centerstudenter, JOVD, Svensk Ungdom, Junge Liberale, Lithuanian Liberal Youth (LLY), Jungfreisinnige Schweiz, JUNOS, CUF, Young Greenliberals Switzerland

Adopted at the Autumn Congress 2023 in Riga, Latvia on 11 November 2023\.

## **Considering that:**

* Per United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8.7, the international community has committed to eradicating forced labour––which remains widespread––by 2030\.

  The	eradication	of	forced	labour	is	also	a	stated	priority	of	the European Union.

  * In  late 2020, the  European  Parliament adopted  a resolution

  (2020/2913(RSP)) acknowledging and condemning China’s government-led system of forced labour and exploitation of Uyghur Muslims while recognising that “the promotion of and respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law should remain at the centre of the long-standing relationship between the EU and China”.

    * Resolution 2020/2913(RSP) noted credible reports of the occurrence of forced labour in the clothing, technology and automotive sectors, stating also that Chinese cotton, 84 percent of which originates from the Xinjiang province, is at particularly high risk of being tainted by forced labour.

    * In 2020, at least 80 international brand-name corporations had been reported to profit, directly or indirectly, from Uyghur forced labour within their supply chains, including many European multinational companies.

    * The European Commission in 2022 proposed legislation prohibiting products made with forced labour on the Union market (COM/2022/453 final). The proposal empowers Member States’ authorities to seize and dispose of products made with forced labour. However, its point-of-departure is ILO’s definition, which addresses commercially motivated cases of forced labour. It does not effectively target politically motivated forced labour, such as that of the Uyghur population in China.

    * COM/2022/453 is complemented by a proposal on corporate sustainability due diligence (COM/2022/71 final). It requires companies to account for and mitigate any adverse impact on human rights within their supply chains. However, the lack of transparency in China, particularly in the Xinjiang province, prevents independent investigations and audits, meaning that there are no reliable means of verifying the absence of forced labour. In addition, regulations would only cover large enterprises over a certain

threshold in terms of number of employees and net turnover, and SMEs over a certain threshold only in “high-impact sectors”.

## **Believing that:**

* The European Commission’s proposals are insufficient to effectively address the entry of products made with forced labour on the Union market.

  * All imports from certain regions and market sectors in China should be presumed to be tainted by forced labour unless proven otherwise.

    * Neither EU Member States nor their citizens should, knowingly or unknowingly, contribute to systematic human rights abuses in China or elsewhere.

    * Per commitments to action set out in its Strategic Framework on Human Rights and Democracy, the EU and its Member States have a responsibility to promote human rights and to prioritize compliance with human rights regulations in all dealings with strategic partners and third countries.

    * A blanket ban would serve to reduce processing times and encourage companies to redirect supply chains to where compliance with human rights regulations can be more effectively ensured.

## **Noting that:**

* In 2020, the U.S. House of Representatives adopted the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA; Public Law No. 117-78), which included a rebuttable ban on imports from the Xinjiang province. The ban has successfully forced companies to reroute their supply chains, and imports from Xinjiang to the U.S. have decreased significantly. However, as a result, imports from the region to the European Union in 2022 jumped by nearly 30 percent, underlining the need for sanction regimes to be consistent in order to be effective.

## **Calls upon:**

* The EU to establish a presumption that products produced wholly or partly in the Xinjiang province of China are tainted by forced labour and thus should be denied entry into the European Union unless evidence is presented to the contrary;

The EU to consider imposing a rebuttable blanket ban on individual market sectors where forced labour is deemed to occur, including but not limited to the clothing, technology and automotive sectors in China as well as those utilizing Chinese cotton,

and to be ready to expand said ban should credible reports of additional regions and sectors tainted by labour force.

66. ##  **Preparing for a Trump Presidency: liberal, rules based order under threat**

(Passed Autumn 2024\)

Mover: Jonge Democraten (Netherlands)

Co-signatories: Alliance Youth, Radikal Ungdom, Young Liberals UK, Centerstudenter, Young Greenliberals (CH), Jongliberalen, LUF, CUF, USR Tineret

Considering that:

* 	Donald Trump has decisively won the US presidential election and the Republican Party has won a majority in both chambers of Congress;

* Donald Trump’s election is expected to have massive consequences for US policy on a wide range of topics that affect the EU and its European allies, such as support for Ukraine & NATO, trade, climate and the protection of democracy, rule of law, and human rights;

* Trump stated he would end the war in Ukraine in 24 hours, raising fears he will pressure Ukraine into unfavourable negotiations with Russia, the country that launched a full-scale, illegal and unjustified war of aggression against it;

* In terms of the US’ economic relationship with the EU, Trump is likely to follow a highly protectionist path, leading to damaging trade frictions between Europe and the US, the world's largest economic relationship;

* Trump indicated that following these elections people ‘wouldn't have to worry about voting again’, indicating his commitment to anti-democratic ideas and the risk that he will place himself above the US constitution, like he tried to do on January 6th 2021, undermining the fundamental principles of democracy;

* Trump withdrew from the Paris agreement in his first term, and is likely to not cooperate on finding sustainable solutions related to the climate crisis, jeopardising the EU's efforts to address this global challenge;

* Trump's ideas are unlikely to be tempered by any advisors willing to contradict him, as his cabinet is expected to be selected based on their loyalty towards

Trump, as indicated by a senior official on Trump’s campaign, leading to a lack of accountability and expertise in US policy-making;

* there is a real risk of the US drastically scaling back its role in European security.

* Currently, European companies in certain sectors are very dependent on US technologies and development, for example in the aerospace and telecommunications sector, where Elon Musk’s SpaceX currently holds a near monopoly for rocket launch technology within the western sphere.

* Elon Musk has played a large part in Donald Trumps presidential election campaign. Donald Trump has even gone as far as offering Elon Musk a potential spot in his administration. Regardless of this, SpaceX has received at least 15.4 billion USD from the US Government in contracts in the last decade. Under a new Trump administration, this number will probably keep going up, thus giving SpaceX an even stronger position in the spacecraft market of the west.

Believing that:

* the EU and its European allies have become dependent across many areas on US action, and won’t be able to rely on US support going forward;

* the EU must take rapid action to ensure its own strategic autonomy and defend its fundamental values and interests;

* the Trump presidency poses a threat to the liberal, rules-based order and the EU needs to take rapid action to protect its values and principles, such as democracy, human rights, and the rule of law;

* liberal youth in Europe need to take a proactive role in ensuring the EU is ready to deal with the effects of a Trump presidency, by advocating for a strong, united EU response that is in line with EU values;

* the EU and its European allies can no longer rely on US support in addressing global challenges and must take concrete steps to ensure its strategic autonomy, even if this means an increase in spending to ensure the defence of the EU’s fundamental values and interests.

* Cybersecurity threats, terrorism threats and information warfare present significant risks to the EU’s security and democratic processes, especially if U.S. intelligence cooperation and support for European cybersecurity decrease under the new administration.

* The EU and the USA share common values \- liberty, rule of law and democracy \- which bind us together in a world threatened by tyranny and which transcend whoever is sitting in the White House or Le Berlaymont.

Calls for:

* a strong, united response from the EU, hand in hand with its European allies, to the challenges posed by a Trump presidency, in defence of the EU’s shared fundamental values and the liberal, rules-based order, including a clear commitment to democracy, human rights, and the rule of law;

* the European Commission to rapidly present its impact assessment of the Trump  
  presidency across all policy files from the perspective of strategic autonomy, and to ensure the Commission is in the position to respond within the first 100 days of its mandate;

* EU and national leaders to establish a functioning working relationship with the incoming US administration to the extent possible, grounded on liberal values and the rules-based international order;

* the European Commission to prepare a strategy for safeguarding European industry

  and business in the event of a protectionist trade war launched by the incoming

  US Administration;

* an urgent increase in European defence spending as well as ramping up of industrial defence production within Europe to ensure its own security as well of that of its allies, most urgently Ukraine, to be able to ensure Europe’s defence and Ukraine’s victory, even without US support, and to ensure that the European aid to Ukraine is structurally increased before President-Elect Trump’s term of office begins;

* an increase in financial support from the EU its Member States and other European states to multilateral institutions, to compensate for the likely decrease in funding to be received from the United States;

* the EU, in close consultation with its European allies, to assume global leadership and collaborate with other countries and international organisations to create a united front on various areas such as climate change while setting ambitious targets to encourage others to follow suit;

* Europe to take over a leading role and do more pioneering work in fighting climate change in order to achieve the global goals set by the Paris agreement also without institutional engagement from the United State;.

* the European Commission, in cooperation with the other European Partners and allies, to develop a comprehensive strategy to counter disinformation, both foreign and domestic, to avoid interference in the EU’s own democratic systems while promoting media literacy, critical thinking, and fact-based journalism

* The European Commission and EU diplomatic representatives to establish and maintain open channels of communication with U.S. sub-federal entities, such as states, municipalities, and cities, as well as other public diplomacy entities such as foundations, universities, NGO’s and civil society organisations, in order to continue collaborative efforts on key issues and shared goals, such as climate change, trade, and human rights, even if cooperation on a federal level declines under the Trump administration.

* The European Commission and EU diplomatic representatives to pursue new frameworks for cooperation with willing non-federal U.S. entities if they align with EU values.

* European companies to increase its efforts and investments into research and development of infrastructural resilience in areas such as the aerospace and telecommunications sector, thereby reducing its dependence on US scientific knowledge, technology and infrastructure.

* The EU must proactively strengthen its intelligence and cybersecurity infrastructure to safeguard against potential foreign interference and cyber threats, ensuring resilience in the face of diminishing external support from the USA.

* The Member States must not only cooperate with the US on the national level but

  on the regional and local level aswell in order to strenghten the bond between our nations, improve mutual understanding and create leverage for future cooperation on a national level.

* The EU and its Member States must work together with the US \- wherever it is possible \- regardless of who is sitting in the White House in order to tackle the common challenges we face.

  67. ##  **When women are forced to silence, liberals speak up**

(Passed Autumn 2024\)

Submitted by: Centerstudenter (Sweden)

MO’s supporting: Unge Venstre (Norway), Alliance Youth (Northern Ireland), Keskustan Opiskelijaliitto (Finland), Keskustanuoret (Finland), LiDeM (North Macedonia), Venstres Ungdom (Denmark), YMRF (Bulgaria), Silvia Fernández (IMS), Liberala Ungdomsförbundet (Sweden), Jonge Democraten (Netherlands), Svensk Ungdom (Finland), Radikal Ungdom (Denmark), Centerpartiets Ungdomsförbund (Sweden), Jonk Demokraten (Luxembourg), Youth Forum of Naša stranka (Bosnia and Herzegovina)

Noting that:

* Since the Taliban seized power in August 2021, women’s rights in Afghanistan have regressed dramatically, undoing decades of progress toward gender equality.

* The European Court of Justice (ECJ) recently ruled that gender and nationality alone are sufficient reasons to grant asylum to Afghan women. Currently, some European countries, such as Bulgaria, provide first-instance protection to as few as 12% of Afghan asylum seekers despite the severity of their situation.

* In Afghanistan over 70 decrees have been enacted during the last three years, excluding women and girls from nearly all aspects of public life and leading to what is being termed as "gender apartheid."

* Girls are banned from schooling beyond 6th grade, and women are barred from most paid employment as well as public spaces such as parks and gyms. They are forced to wear full-body coverings and cover their faces. Women are not even allowed to speak in public any more.

* More than one million school-aged girls—80%—are out of school, with dire consequences for future generations, including a projected 50% increase in early childbearing and maternal mortality.

* In 2023, 28.7% of Afghan girls under 18 were married and 9.6% under the age of 15\.

* The Taliban have openly stated that the ideal situation is for women to avoid leaving their homes entirely, unless absolutely necessary. This forced isolation is driving many women and girls into deep despair with increasing suicide attempts.

* The Taliban's new self-proclaimed ‘Ministry of Virtue and Vice’ has tortured women protesters with electric shocks, with reports of rape in custody, and their highest leader has announced the reintroduction of public flogging and stoning for adultery.

* Believing that:

* The brutality of the Taliban’s rule mandates the European countries to act immediately and protect Afghan women that escaped the regime.

* The rise of anti-refugee rhetoric in Europe \- also amongst ALDE member parties

  \- ridicules the serious reality of Afghan refugees and counteracts integration efforts whilst it strengthens the European far-right and nationalist forces.

Therefore, LYMEC calls for:

* Immediate improvement of first-instance protection for Afghan women in Europe.

* ALDE members to stand firm against fundamentalism and the far right, recognize the harsh reality of women that escaped Afghanistan and return to a rhetoric that promotes the open society and a moral Europe.

* Targeted sanctions against Taliban leaders responsible for human rights abuses, and support for international legal accountability.

* A strong stance by EU countries in international forums, such as the United Nations, condemning the abuse of Afghan women’s rights.

* Increased efforts to return Afghan girls to school.

* Avoidance of using Taliban terminology, such as the "Ministry of Virtue."

* Gender Equality Initiatives, in the context of feminist development cooperation, should be an important pillar of international aid to Afghanistan. Donors who engage in development cooperation with Afghanistan need to ensure that their projects don't fund the Taliban regime.

  68. ##  **Accelerated pathway for Ukrainian EU membership**

(Passed Autumn 2024\)

Submitted by: Liberal Youth of Sweden (LUF), Unge Venstre (NUV), Radikal Ungdom (RU), ZeMolodizhka

Co-signed by: Jonge Democraten, Młodzi Nowoczesní, Centerstudenter, Junge Liberale, Svensk Ungdom, CUF

Keywords: Ukraine, EU membership, gradual integration, observer status Recognising that:  
Russia's full-scale unprovoked aggression against Ukraine, as of 24 February, 2022, appeared to become a watershed pivotal point, after which the growing danger for the existence of liberal democracies can no longer be ignored;

Following the brutal invasion by the Russian Federation into Ukraine, the resilient Ukrainian people have not only defended their homeland but also safeguarded the values and democracy of the entirety of Europe;

Ukraine has made significant progress towards EU membership after obtaining candidate status on 17 June 2022, and maintains a high pace of reform towards EU convergence

Believing that:

The EU has an obligation to maintain a strong support for Ukraine as much as it takes for as long as needed;

Sending more military, humanitarian and economic aid is essential in supporting Ukraine;

Political support of Ukraine also is of the highest importance, such as promoting Ukraine’s rightful place within the European Union;

Ukraine can and must win the war, why the EU and its global allies need to provide sufficient and timely support for as long as it might take; to withstand Russian offensives, liberate its citizens and territories, deter the aggressor from new strikes, and punish all those guilty of crimes against humanity and law, to rebuild and revive the country;

LYMEC calls for:

Enhanced economic and trade relations between the EU and Ukraine, leading towards Ukraine’s full integration into EU’s Internal Market;

Allowing Ukraine to participate as full members in further EU cooperation areas, as soon as the corresponding negotiation chapter is closed;

Granting Ukraine observer status within the EU institutions, among other things by expanding the opportunities for officials from Ukraine to observe the work within EU institutions.

Renewing the basic principles of the EU Enlargement policy: Whilst ensuring strict compliance with criteria for EU accession, new frameworks of cooperation with EU candidate and EU neighbouring countries, in particular should be established as a matter of priority to guarantee a stable EU political and economic system and also connect third countries more closely with the EU to prevent other geopolitical forces from gaining too much influence, such as but not limited to Russia and China.

69. ##  **The case Moldova: Russian meddling in European democracies, time to act**

(Passed Autumn 2024\)

Submitted by: Jongliberalen (JL, former Jong VLD), Jungfreisinnige Schweiz (JFS) Co-signers: Jeunes MR (JMR), Joventut Nacionalista de Catalunya (JNC), Alliance  
Youth, Youth Movement for Rights and Freedoms (YMRF), Radikal Ungdom (RU), Psg

Youth, Nowoczesna Youth (NY), Unge Venstre (NUV), USR Tineret, ZeMolodizhka, Junge Liberale (JuLis), Svensk Ungdom (SU), Estonian Reform Party Youth, JUNOS.

Title: The case Moldova: Russian meddling in European democracies, time to act Noting that:

* Russia attempted to subvert the recent 2024 Moldovan referendum on European Union membership and the 2024 Moldovan presidential election;

* Russia specifically sought to influence Moldovans to vote against EU membership and the pro-European candidate, Maia Sandu, by offering payments totaling 39 million USD through an internationally sanctioned Russian bank to over 130,000 recipients, according to prosecutors;

* The outcome of the presidential election in Moldova was a clear commitment of the Moldovan people to freedom, democracy, and European integration despite Russian meddling;

* The recent re-election of Donald Trump as US president is posing a tremendous threat to the military security and stability of Europe and the world;

* Russia's influence in Europe is on the rise;

* Several political actors in Moldova disingenuously pretended to be pro-European but campaigned against the recent referendum;

* In the run-off to the second round of elections, bomb threats made it difficult for voters abroad to cast their votes;

* Volunteers got threatened while campaigning;

* Undercover investigation from the Moldovan newspaper ‘Ziarul de Gardă’ clearly unveiled deep ties between Ilan Șor and the Kremlin in their ‘În slujba Moscovei’ report.

* Russia is illegally occupying part of Moldova, and that any attempts to negotiate the withdrawal of its so-called "peace keepers" have failed because of Russia acting aggressively, illegally and in bad-faith

Pointing out that:

* There is an immediate risk of further escalation in the Russian war on Ukraine if

  U.S. military aid were to end under a potential new Trump administration.;

* Moldava is one of the main targets of Russian foreign interference;

* At the same time as the first round of the presidential election, in a referendum held at the same time, the country's EU membership was enshrined in the constitution as a national objective by a narrow majority.

Believing that:

* Moldova belongs with the rest of democratic Europe and the free world, standing united in shared values and aspirations;

* Freedom, democracy, and rule of law are necessary conditions to ensure the respect of human rights;

* Election interference of all kinds—internal or external—are hindering democratic decision making processes.

LYMEC to call for:

* European Governments to support the Moldovan government in its efforts to strengthen democracy and the rule of law in the country;

* The EU to help the further integration of the Republic of Moldova into the European contractual framework;

* The EU to acknowledge the will of the Moldovan people to join the Union;

* Reducing tariffs in order to strengthen economic ties between Europe and Moldova (and therefore reducing the dependency on Russia) through trade and lifting visa restrictions for Moldovan citizens.

* European Governments to recognize and support Maia Sandu’s presidential election victory;

* Liberal political and civil society organisations in Moldova to aid the pro-European government in Chisinau and Maia Sandu in combating Russian influence and in enforcing reforms that will align the country with European standards;

* The European Union, in tandem with Moldovan authorities, to expand communication campaigns to raise public awareness of the benefits of EU integration for Moldova and to promote understanding of the challenges, including Russian interference;

* The European Union to strengthen technical and advisory assistance to help Moldova navigate accession negotiations and manage the substantial workload as Moldova works towards EU integration.

* Support for Republic of Moldova’s goal to join the EU by 2030

* The EU and its Member States to assist Moldova in creating and implementing a long-term plan for peace, stability, economic prosperity and international rules-based order in Transnistria

* ALDE Party and LYMEC MOs to help lobby for European Acquis Communautaire and provide the necessary political support for Republic of Moldova's European integration

  70. ##  **Stop teaching hate: End of genocide denial in European classrooms**

(Passed Autumn 2024\)

Submitted by: Youth Forum of Naša stranka (Bosnia and Herzegovina)

MO’s supporting the Resolution: Youth MRF (Bulgaria), Mladi HNS-a (Croatia), Mladi hrvatski liberali (Croatia), Jonge Democraten (the Netherlands), Alliance Youth (Northern Ireland), Young Progressive Slovakia (Slovakia), Gibanje svoboda mladi (Slovenia), Centerstudenter (Sweden), Young Green Liberals (Switzerland), Young Liberals (United Kingdom),

Considering that:

* Article 26 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights ensures that everyone has the right to education and that education shall be directed to the full development of the human personality and the strengthening of respect for human rights and fundamental freedom

* The International Court of Justice determined in 2007 that the acts committed in Srebrenica during the Bosnian war constituted acts of genocide.

* The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) has found former leaders of Bosnian Serbs Radovan Karadžić and Ratko Mladić guilty for their roles in genocide, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity and sentenced them to life imprisonment.

* The Pedagogical Institute of Republika Srpska entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina has revised the primary school history curriculum which now presents Radovan Karadžić and Ratko Mladić as historical figures who held important military and political positions rather than war criminals.

* The denial of genocide, as an attempt to deny or minimize the scale and severity of an instance of genocide, is an integral part of genocide

Noting that:

* The Resolution 2574 (2024) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe on Bosnia and Herzegovina encourages the establishment of a common core curriculum in history allowing for all to understand the diversity of points of view while prohibiting the honoring in the school curriculums of individuals convicted of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.

* The Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina temporarily suspended a part of the primary school curriculum in Republika Srpska entity of Bosnia and

Herzegovina presenting individuals convicted of war criminals as historic figures.

* The OSCE mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina has criticized these changes in curriculum stating that they threaten critical reforms in history teaching, perpetuate divisions, and obscure the complex roots of the violence.

Recognizing that:

* The educational systems should be unbiased and should not deepen the divisions, teach intolerance, and promote genocide denialism or glorification of convicted war criminals.

* The true reconciliation and long-lasting peace in the Western Balkans can be achieved only if the truth about the atrocities and war crimes is taught in an objective and unbiased way

* The European Union has a role in promoting peace, ensuring tolerance, and protecting human rights.

* Therefore, LYMEC calls for:

* Condemnation of the new school curriculums in Republika Srpska entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina which honor individuals convicted of genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes.

* Developing appropriate educational programs in the European Union that would ensure teaching about the Srebrenica genocide and prevent future instances of genocide glorification or denial.

* Introducing stricter standards towards aspiring European Union member countries that would ensure that their school curriculums, textbooks, and educational materials do not honor, celebrate, or glorify sentenced war criminals.

  71. ##  **For a Free Tibet**

(Passed Spring 2025\)

Submitted by: Junge Liberale (JuLis)

Co-signed by: Bundesverband Liberaler Hochschulgruppen (LHG), CUF, ERPY, JNC, Jonge Democraten, JOVD, Jungfreisinnige Schweiz, JUNOS, Lithuanian Liberal Youth,

LUF, Nowoczesna Youth, Radikale Ungdom, Venstres Ungdom, Young Liberals UK, Molodezhka

Considering that:

* The worsening human rights situation in Tibet, particularly the Tibetan Autonomous Region (TAR). Including reports of arbitrary arrests, unfair trials, inhumane detention conditions, and torture.  
* The absence of freedom of expression in Tibet, particularly in the TAR.

* The absence of freedom of religion in Tibet, particularly in the TAR.

* The absence of freedom of movement in Tibet, particularly in the TAR.

* The imperial language policy of the People's Republic of China, which increasingly sidelines the Tibetan language in public life within Tibet, particularly in the TAR.

* Reports of the planned constructions of water dams and reservoirs in populated areas of the Tibetan high plateau and the danger of ecological disasters.  
* The potential cutoff of water-flows in rivers originating in the Tibetan high plateau for downstream riparian countries in Southeast Asia and South Asia.  
* The restrictions on reports and expressions regarding Tibet on Chinese media and social media, including Chinese owned enterprises which operate abroad, such as TikTok.  
* The official discourse of the PRC which has replaced the term Tibet with the sinicized term “Xizang” in its official documents and statements concerning Tibet.

Believing that:

* In the future of a free and democratic Tibet.

* Freedom of speech, freedom of expression, freedom of religion and freedom of movement are fundamental human rights, which no human being shall be restricted from exercising.

* The Tibetan language, as other regional languages in the PRC, should be a language of instruction in schools.

* The Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), its democratically elected representatives – including the Sikyong and the members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-exile – is a torchbearer for Tibetan democracy.

* The CTA should see increasing global support for its cause to resolve the Tibet conflict in a peaceful manner, according to the right of self-determination.

* The CTA is the only authority, as the democratic representation of Tibetans around the world, which shall negotiate the issue of Tibet with the government of the PRC.

* The current “Umaylam” (Middle-Way Approach) is a suitable option to restore peace and dignity to Tibetans living in Tibet, especially those living in the TAR, as long as it is the Tibetans.  
* The EU should voice their support for the cause of the CTA, vis-à-vis the government of the PRC.

Emphasizing that:

* Tibet – including the TAR and parts of Qinghai, Sichuan and Yunnan – is an independent country under occupation of the PRC since 1950\.

* Historical Tibet – before 1950 – has been an independent country which exercised diplomatic relations with other countries.

* The illegal annexation of Tibet by the forces of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) of the PRC was a grave violation of international law, for which the PRC has never had to take responsibility.

* The institution of the Dalai Lama – including the current 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyaltso – is of invaluable importance for the Tibetan people.

LYMEC thus calls for:

* The EU and its member states to clearly condemn the human rights violations in the TAR and Tibetan regions of Qinghai, Sichuan and Yunnan. Political asylum must be granted to dissidents from Tibet.

* The EU and its member states to maintain a regular dialogue with the exiled representatives of the CTA, especially the Sikyong and the members of the Kashag and the Tibet Bureau in Brussels.

* The EU to acknowledge the Middle-Way Approach to seek a peaceful solution to the Tibet conflict.

* The EU to acknowledge the status of Tibet as an independent country before the illegal annexation of the PRC.

* The European Parliament to send a delegation of parliamentarians to the Tibetan Parliament-in-exile.

* The EU to only support the legitimacy of religious reincarnations of Tibetan religious institutions, such as the Dalai Lama or Panchen Lama, which have been approved by the legitimate democratic representation of the Tibetan people, which is the CTA.  
* The EU and its member states to advocate internationally for the continued public teaching of Tibetan in Tibetan schools in the PRC.  
* The EU and its member states to condemn any threats of public bans of the Tibetan language.  
* The EU and its member states to voice their concern, regarding the transnational effects in Southeast Asia and South Asia due to PRC-led construction projects that would affect the flow of water in rivers originating in the Tibetan high plateau.  
* The EU and its member states support the U.S. “Reciprocal access to Tibet Act” and to implement legislation following the U.S. “Reciprocal Access to Tibet Act”.

* Free access to the TAR and adjacent Tibetan settlements, including the freedom of movement for Tibetans.

* All internationally recognized NGOs be granted access to Tibet and not be hindered in their work. NGOs, particularly those not recognized under Chinese national law but recognized internationally, should be included.

* Representatives of the press must be granted unlimited access to Tibet. Government censorship, influence, or intimidating surveillance of the press must be stopped.

* Diplomatic personnel from the European Union and its member states must be granted unlimited access to Tibet.

* Any official responsible for denying access should be denied entry to the European Union under the principle of diplomatic reciprocity. This applies only to employees and officials of the Chinese authorities. Employees of the Chinese press, Chinese NGOs, or Chinese private individuals should not be affected by this regulation.

* The High Representative and either the European External Action Service or the European Union Institute for Security Studies should produce an annual report on access possibilities for the above-mentioned groups to Tibet, naming those responsible for denying entry.

  72. ##  **Secure the Eastern Flank: Secure the Union**

(Passed Spring 2025\)

Secure the Eastern Flank: Secure the Union

Submitted by: USR Tineret, Liberal Democratic League of Ukraine, Nowoczesna Youth Co-signed by: JUNOS, Arthur Wu (IMS), Young Progressive Slovakia, European Youth of Ukraine, Adam Volf (IMS), Young Liberals, Molodezhka, Attistibai Youth, Alliance Youth, Lithuanian Liberal Youth, Jonge Democraten, Youth Forum of Naša stranka, Jongliberalen, Junge Liberale, JOVD

*Considering that:*

* The European Union faces a growing security threat from external adversaries, including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. Russia's continued aggression, exemplified by its war in Ukraine, challenges regional stability, while China's economic and cyber influence poses strategic risks. Iran's support for proxy groups and its deepening ties with Russia further destabilize the security landscape. Additionally, North Korean troops have reportedly been deployed near the EU's eastern border, escalating concerns over military threats;  
* Eastern European countries are the first line of defence against Russian aggression, as well as under the most significant and immediate threat of both hybrid and conventional attacks;  
* Russia has openly demanded the re-establishment of NATO’s borders to a pre-2004 configuration, posing a direct threat to the sovereignty and security of Eastern European nations and undermining the stability of the region;  
* Conflicts, external interferences and general instability in Eastern Europe directly affects all of Europe;  
* The European continent is not only affected by conventional attacks, but also by hybrid warfare tactics. Eastern European countries are particularly targeted by these hybrid threats, which remain largely unaddressed;

* Europe has seen a surge of disinformation campaigns, especially focused on raising ultra nationalist, isolationist and revanchist sentiments, aimed at compromising European security and solidarity from within;

* The omnipresent foreign disinformation, misinformation and propaganda are undermining Europe’s firm support for Ukraine;

* The phenomenon of isolationism is perilously becoming the new core of the Euro-Atlantic policy of the United States of America \- Europe’s most crucial ally;

* Outside of the European Union, Europe also is home to three other prominent NATO members \- the United Kingdom, Norway and Türkiye

* Whilst the European Union is home to several of the world's most innovative and prestigious defence firms, only two EU based contractors are in the world's top 30 largest defence firms.

*Believing that:*

* In 2025, we are witnessing powerful international actors engaging in politics meant to change the rules-based international order which existed from WW2 onwards;  
* Traditional partners of European countries engaging in bullying behavior is a strong signal that Europeans should further consolidate their own common security;

* There is virtually and literally no chance of European countries tackling security challenges each on their own, and challenges present themselves in a rather near than distant future;

* In a world where powerful international actors are engaging in politics meant to change the rules-based international order, there is a grave and immediate threat to European democracy and to European liberalism;  
* External actors are pursuing an aggressive disinformation campaign against the European Union and its Member States, bordering on actions of hybrid warfare, in order to delegitimize their institutions, attack their common values, weaken their sense of solidarity and undermine European security;

* The treaties on Good-Neighbourliness, Friendly Relations, and Cooperation signed between former Warsaw Pact member states following the fall of the Iron Curtain were essential instruments for maintaining regional stability, fostering diplomatic cooperation, and promoting economic and social ties. These treaties serve as a foundation for conflict prevention, minority rights protection, and peaceful coexistence in Eastern Europe;  
* Relying too heavily upon non-European security firms and externally sourced intelligence compromises Europe’s ability to defend itself;  
* The European Union is the world’s second largest economy and, thus, must be capable of defending itself, especially in case of military aggression;  
* Eastern European security is European security;

* A divided Europe is a weak Europe.

*Welcomes:*

* The EU’s recent “ReArm Europe” plan;

* The efforts made by European countries in supporting Ukraine obtain a just and lasting peace;

* The 12 Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) Members commitment to collaboration in keeping the Eastern Flank of Europe safe through joint exercises and intelligence sharing.

*Calls for:*

* All EU Member States to reaffirm their commitment to the mutual defence clause of the European Union (Article 42.7 of the Treaty of the European Union);

* The strengthening of joint military-technological cooperation, security and innovation; the European Union must prioritize collaborative defence research, weapons development, and cybersecurity advancements. This effort should integrate lessons learned from the battlefield experience of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, ensuring that emerging military technologies are battle-tested, adaptable, and capable of countering evolving threats;  
* European countries to up their budgetary allowances towards defence, be it into the military, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure or technology which could serve for deterrence and defence purposes;  
* The EU to urgently allocate funds and create funding mechanisms to be used for defence spending and investment, especially towards bolstering the security of the Union’s Eastern Flank;  
* European countries to ensure that Ukraine and the rest of the European allies have access to high-level military intelligence and counterintelligence resources, and that their intelligence and counterintelligence efforts are developed in collaboration with trustworthy non-European and international partners who share their values.  
* The European Union to consider further advanced cooperation with democratic partners and strategic allies sharing mutual international values.  
* All EU member states to compliment the joint procurement strategy of ‘ReArm’ through encouraging defence and security firms to further collaborate across borders, and consider consolidating into larger companies;  
* Eastern European countries to enhance regional cooperation in order to address present and future security threats. This should include not only conventional defence but also prevention of cyber attacks, political and electoral interference, energy shortages and any other areas necessary for maintaining the peace and security of the region;  
* European countries in general and (non-aggressor) Eastern European countries in particular to stand together against foreign actors trying to pit them against one another. Any and all attempts to divide or isolate us need to be met with united, unwavering opposition;  
* European countries which are not currently JEF members to explore funding and collaboration with JEF in order to help deter any potential Russian aggression along Europe's North-Eastern borders;

* ALDE and its member parties to condemn any and all attempts to sabotage friendly relations and cooperation between (non-aggressor) Eastern European countries and reaffirm support for good-neighbourliness, friendly relations, and cooperation in the region;

* The B9 (Bucharest Nine) countries to integrate Ukraine into the format;

* All European countries to continue to support Ukraine;

* The European Commission to allocate additionals funds for Poland’s East Shield initiative and other similar Eastern Flank defence projects;

* All European nations to raise defence spending over the 2% of GDP target, starting 2026\.

  73. ##  **In solidarity with the people of Georgia**

(Passed Spring 2025\) Submitted by: CUF

Co-signers: Alliance Youth, Unge Venstre, Nowoczesna Youth, Molodezhka, Venstres Ungdom, Svensk Ungdom, ERPY, Youth Forum of Naša stranka, JeunesMR, Silvia Fernández (IMS), HSLS, Lithuanian Liberal Youth, LUF, Centerstudenter.

*Noting that:*

* In October 2024 elections were held in Georgia. Many called for a re-run due to significant irregularities, among them the EU parliament who declared the election as neither free nor fair.  
* Georgian Dream declared themselves the winner, and no new election has been held.  
* The government has delayed the country’s EU membership bid until 2028\.

* In September 2024, Georgia’s parliament recently approved new legislation decreasing LGBTQIA+ rights.  
* The bill seeks to ban rights such as same-sex marriage, adoption by same-sex couples and gender-affirming care.  
* Several European countries still list Georgia as a safe country of origin.  
* Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights guarantees the right to respect for private and family life, free from unnecessary state interference.

* LYMEC has previously addressed the European perspective for Georgia and called for closer cooperation with civil society in its resolution “Closing Putin's gates means welcoming allies \- Extending an invitation to Georgia”;

*Considering that:*

* An overwhelming majority (over 80%) of Georgian citizens support EU membership.  
* Pro-LGBTQIA+ organizations in Georgia, who already face difficult circumstances, have indicated that the new laws would force them to shut down.  
* Lists of safe countries of origin exist to speed up asylum applications, putting Georgian LGBTQIA+ asylum seekers at risk for deportation.

* Only a day after the so-called ‘family values’ bill was passed, one of the first openly trans public figures in Georgia, Kesaria Abramidze, was murdered in her home.

* Hundreds of people protesting the government have been arrested, and among them more than 300 have suffered torture, beatings and other ill-treatment from law enforcement (according to Amnesty International).  
* In February 2025 49 opposition MPs were expelled from Parliament by the government.  
* EU funding to Georgia has mainly focused on economic development to raise quality of life for citizens.

* This EU assistance is conditional, leading to funds being frozen or stopped due to democratic backsliding.

* According to CNN, the US’ freeze in foreign aid has damaged civil society and independent media in Georgia.

*Believing that:*

* One of the ways the EU can promote democracy and human rights in Georgia is to support the local organizations working to uphold these values.

* Independent media and civil society are two cornerstones of democracy.

* While EU funds in general should continue to be strictly conditional on democratic progress, we should do more to support independent media and civil society in Georgia directly.  
* The so-called Family Values bill will undermine the fundamental rights of the Georgian people, while increasing discrimination, stigmatization and violence against LGBTQIA+ people.

* LGBTQIA+ people are not safe to be living freely without persecution in Georgia.

* Georgia is no longer fit to be on any European country’s safe state list.

*We therefore call for:*

* LYMEC to condemn the so-called Family Values bill.

* EU member states and representatives to maintain pressure on Georgia to withdraw the legislation.  
* The EU to offer financial aid to independent media and civil society in Georgia that maintain democratic values.  
* All EU member states to immediately remove Georgia from their safe state lists.  
* All EU member states and European States to impose Visa sanctions on members of the Georgian Dream government responsible for the attack on human rights in Georgia

  74. ##  **Resolution on Strengthening EU Foreign Aid to Countries in Crisis**

(Passed Spring 2025\) Submitted by: CUF

*Noting that:*

* In recent years, global political instability, economic hardships, and humanitarian crises have increased, exacerbating challenges for vulnerable populations.

* The growing risks posed by novel security threats such as climate breakdown, disease outbreaks, and global famine are not going away and cannot be tackled through conventional military means alone.  
* The temporary suspension of foreign aid by the United States has further strained humanitarian efforts and weakened support for civil society organizations working to protect human rights and democratic values.

* American withdrawal and the shutting down of USAID will have dire consequences for many countries around the world, particularly in the health sector.

* Development Cooperation presents one of the strongest tools to exercise soft power.

* The dismantling of aid structures occurs rapidly, while rebuilding them is a long and challenging process.

* Some countries are particularly vulnerable due to prolonged conflict, political instability, and ongoing humanitarian crises, making external aid crucial for grassroots organizations, refugee support systems, and post-conflict reconstruction.  
* Without sustainable financial support, civil society organizations in crisis-affected nations risk collapse, threatening the protection of fundamental freedoms and human rights.  
* Hostile state governments, such as Russia and China, have used gaps in international development funding as opportunities to build ties with developing nations and exploit their resources.

*Considering that:*

* The EU has a long-standing commitment to promoting democracy, human rights, and development aid worldwide.

* There is growing recognition that international development funding has an important security dimension by tackling emerging risks and novel security threats  
* The reduction of aid from individual member states has created an urgent need for the EU to step up and fill the gap.  
* The EU has the capacity to compensate for national aid reductions and reinforce its role as a global leader in humanitarian and development assistance.  
* Local organizations are often best placed to ensure aid is effectively utilized and directly benefits those in need.  
* A long-term and predictable approach to aid is necessary to allow organizations to plan and implement sustainable development initiatives.  
* Any gap in international development funding which allows Russia or China to gain a foothold in key geopolitical regions is a threat to the security interests of the EU and European states.

*Believing that:*

* The EU must acknowledge the significant role of development aid in stabilizing regions affected by conflict, poverty, and human rights violations, as well as the role it plays in preventing future security threats.

* The reduction of aid contributions from individual member states should be counterbalanced by a stronger collective effort at the EU level.  
* Targeted support for local organizations ensures that financial resources reach those most in need and strengthens resilience in fragile regions.  
* EU aid efforts must prioritise those nations where the withdrawal of support from individual countries has left crucial civil society organizations and humanitarian programs in jeopardy.  
* Strengthening the EU’s global leadership in aid policies is crucial to upholding commitments to human rights, peace, and democracy.  
* EU allies in geopolitical regions which benefit from international development funding can have a key role in supporting the delivery of aid and tackling novel security threats, and European states must take opportunities to build relationships with these allies as equal partners  
* Whilst increases to defence spending are necessary, these increases should not be funded through cuts to international development aid as this limits Europe's ability to address novel security threats and prevent future security challenges.

*We therefore call for:*

* The EU and partner European states to increase funding for international aid to compensate for national reductions and prevent the deterioration of human rights conditions in affected regions.

* EU member states to devote at least 0.7 percent of their GDP for development cooperation, in line with the UN target for developed economies.

* The EU and partner European states to prioritize financial support for local organizations working on the ground in authoritarian regimes and conflict zones.

* The EU and partner European states to allocate sustained and increased financial support to countries where the withdrawal of aid has left a dangerous gap in humanitarian assistance and democratic rebuilding efforts.

* The EU and European partner states to adopt a long-term strategy for humanitarian and development assistance, ensuring stable and predictable commitments.  
* The EU and partner European states to find alternate ways to fund increases in defence spending instead of cutting overseas development funding  
* The EU to reinforce its global leadership in aid policies, ensuring that vital humanitarian efforts are not compromised by reductions in bilateral aid contributions.  
* The EU to carefully ensure that its development cooperation and international partnerships are subject to strict policy standards in line with the EU's

Common Security and Defence Policy, hence minimizing the danger of wasteful spending and spending that disregards the EU´s global interests

75. ##  **Standing up for Justice: Supporting the Serbian Student Protests**

(Passed Spring 2025\)

Submitted by: Youth Forum of Naša stranka (Bosnia and Herzegovina), Liberalno Demokratska Mladina (North Macedonia), Mladi hrvatski liberali (Croatia), Mladi HNS-a (Croatia), Mladi liberali Crne Gore (Montenegro), Gibanje Svoboda Mladi (Slovenia), USR Tineret (Romania), YMRF (Bulgaria)  
Cosigned by: Jeunes MR (Belgium), Jongliberalen (Belgium), Joventut Nacionalista de Catalunya (Catalonia), Venstres Ungdom (Denmark), Bundesverband Liberaler Hochschulgruppen (Germany), JOVD (the Netherlands), Alliance Youth (Northern Ireland), Young Green Liberals (Switzerland), Young Liberals (United Kingdom)

*Considering that:*

* On 1 November 2024, the canopy of Novi Sad railway station collapsed causing the deaths of 15 people including two children  
* The railway station in Novi Sad was reconstructed by the Ministry of Construction, Transportation, and Infrastructure and opened just four months before the collapse  
* The Government of Serbia has not taken any responsibility for the tragedy and has repeatedly falsely stated that the collapsed canopy was not part of the reconstruction  
* The lack of a response from the Government and the reluctance of the Prosecutor’s office to do a full investigation in this case has caused university students to start a blockade of faculties across the country

*Noting that:*

* Around 75% of the state-owned faculties in Serbia are currently under blockade

* A significant number of high schools, some elementary schools, and preschool institutions have also followed the blockade of their activities

* The political situation in Serbia has become increasingly polarised which escalated with protests in the National Assembly and multiple city assemblies around the country  
* The current student protests have been the biggest gathering of citizens of Serbia since the 5 October 2000 protests that led to the overthrowing of the regime of Slobodan Milošević

* Student protests in Serbia have inspired similar student protests in the neighboring countries including Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro, Slovenia, and North Macedonia but also throughout the Serbian diaspora in Europe and the rest of the world

* Numerous instances of violence against peaceful protestors have been recorded including physical attacks with baseball bats, multiple car

rammings targeting protestors, and arbitrary detentions as intimidation tactics by authorities

*Recognizing that:*

* The citizen protests are the cornerstone of every functioning liberal democracy

* The freedom of assembly and peaceful protest are fundamental rights that are protected under European and international law

* The actions of the Government of Serbia contradict fundamental European values and have been undermining its path of becoming a member of the European Union

* The Prosecutor’s office still hasn’t fully investigated all of the details of the canopy collapse and indicted all of the people responsible for this tragedy

* A significant number of professional organizations, cultural institutions, athletes, and artists from Serbia and the wider region have supported the student protest

*Therefore, LYMEC calls for:*

* Supporting the right of Serbian students to protest peacefully, free from intimidation, violence, and political persecution

* ALDE Party and Renew Europe to give full support to the student protests, condemn the violence against the students, and request the respect of the rule of law in Serbia  
* The Government of Serbia to fulfill the demands of the students to the fullest including publishing all of the documentation concerning the collapse of the canopy at Novi Sad Railway Station, indicting those who are responsible for the collapse, identifying and punishing people responsible for the attacks on students and citizens who were demonstrating, dropping charges against people arrested at the protests and a greater budget allocations for education  
* The European Commission to put pressure on the Government of Serbia to fulfill all the student demands  
* The European Commission and European Council to ensure that all of the countries seeking membership in the European Union have the highest level of respect for individual freedoms and human rights, ensure full protection of the right to protest in line with EU standards, and ensure transparent, accountable governance in line with European democratic principles

  76. ##  **A coalition of the trading; leading by example**

(Passed Spring 2025\)

Co-Signers: JNC, For Youth\! (Latvia), JUNOS, Jongerenorganisatie Vrijheid en Democratie, Jongliberalen, Venstres Ungdom, Silvia Fernandez (IMS), Radikal Ungdom (RU), Junge Liberale (JuLis), USR Tineret, Centerstudenter (CS), LHG, Norges Unge Venstre (NUV)

*Noting that:*

* the European Union is an actor that largely relies on soft power and international law on the global stage;

* a trade war is looming due to the unproved policy decisions of the Trump administration in the US;

* a policy of imposing incredibly high tariffs on all trade has historically clearly been economically detrimental to all parties;

* the Appellate Body of the World Trade Organization has since 2019 been unable to properly exercise its role as a protector of trade agreements, since the US has been blocking new appointments to it, resulting in it being unable to enforce WTO rules and punish violators of WTO rules,  
* where the EU has exclusive competence, meaning that only the EU can legislate on the issue and not the Member States, the EU alone has the power to negotiate and conclude an international agreement on the matter;

* where an international agreement also covers shared competences, where the Member States has the competence until there is EU legislation on the matter, the agreement becomes a so called ‘mixed agreement’ requiring not only the EU to conclude the agreement, but also each Member State to sign and ratify the treaty;

* this mixed trade agreement structure is currently required for agreements that cover elements such as intellectual property rights, social policy and consumer protection, Foreign Direct Investment beyond liberalization and other elements common in comprehensive trade agreements;

* there is a large amount of mixed agreements, that would significantly expand the opportunities for free trade for the EU, finalised or even signed by the EU that have not yet entered into force in large part because difficulty of getting it ratified by every single Member State;  
* the requirement of unanimity in the Council on certain trade agreements further complicates the matter of EU international agreements.

*Believing that:*

* more and freer trade is beneficial for the welfare of all countries involved, and can, when coupled with the right political and diplomatic cooperation, significantly strengthen the ties between free and democratic nations, as the EU itself has shown;

* in a world that seems to be turning back to trade wars and mercantilism, the EU, as a champion of free trade, should be seeking to turning the tide;  
* More access to non-US markets and giving more access to non-US markets can not only fill any potential gaps in loss of opportunity created by reduced free access between the EU and US markets, but can also create more economic opportunities;

* elements such as intellectual property rights, social policy and consumer protection, and Foreign Direct Investment beyond liberalization can be essential and desirable elements of comprehensive trade agreements;

* the EU makes itself a less attractive international partner with its current confusing system of mixed trade agreements, as well as the requirement of unanimity in the Council, since this might mean that even after all parties have spent decades concluding the agreement it can still become wasted effort;

*Calls for:*

* all EU Member States to rapidly ratify the existing trade agreements already signed by the European Union, particularly CETA.

* a rapid signing of the EU free trade agreements with Mercosur and Mexico, followed by a rapid ratification by all Member States should they be classified as mixed agreements;  
* the EU to rapidly pursue more and freer trade agreements, particularly with free and democratic countries or countries on a clear path to becoming freer and more democratic, be those agreements bilateral or multilateral;  
* the EU to intensify its cooperation in these matters with free and democratic partners, like Canada and Mexico, that have been unprovokedly and unfairly targeted by immense tariffs by the US;  
* the EU, its Member States and European states to work on reforming the WTO so that it can effectively function as a protector of trade, as well as no longer being able to be paralysed by the actions or inactions by one state or a small group of states;  
* the Treaties of the European Union to be revised so that international agreements can cover both exclusive as well as shared competences and still fall within the full competence of the EU, and thus not requiring the mixed agreement process;

* the Treaties of the European Union to be revised so that all international agreements concluded by the EU require Qualified Majority Voting when being voted on by the Council, in line with our position all votes taken by the European Council currently taken by unanimity should be taken by, at the very most, Qualified Majority Voting instead.

  77. ##  **End the Systemic Corruption: Justice for Victims of Kočani Tragedy**

(Passed Spring 2025\)

Submitted by: Liberalno Demokratska Mladina (North Macedonia)

MO’s supporting the Resolution: Youth Forum of Naša stranka (Bosnia and Herzegovina), Young Liberals (United Kingdom), USR Tineret (Romania), HNS Youth (Croatia), Youth Movement for Rights and Freedom (Bulgaria), LHG Youth (Germany), JUNOS (Austria), Venstres Ungdom VU (Denmark), Joventut Nacionalista de Catalunya (Catalonia)

*Considering that:*

* On 16 March 2025, there was a deadly fire in the town of Kočani in the nightclub „Pulse“ causing 59 deaths and over 180 injured victims. This was the deadliest fire incident in the history of North Macedonia.

* The nightclub, which was formerly used as a carpet warehouse, was unlicensed and broke numerous safety standards: it lacked sprinklers, sufficient emergency exits, and it only had a single fire extinguisher, amongst other things

* Widespread corruption was one of the major contributing factors to this disaster since this led to a lack of public oversight and proper safety inspections, which could have prevented this kind of disaster.  
* The lack of accountability and possible pressure on the state public prosecutor to lead the investigation in favor of the current Government has caused people across the country to protest and go on marches, the biggest of which was organized by the movement „Koj e sleden?“ (Who is next?)

*Noting that:*

* According to the Government of North Macedonia, out of 50 establishments of this nature in the whole country, only 22 have the legal licenses to work.

* The political situation in North Macedonia has become increasingly polarized, with citizens demanding to reopen investigations into incidents of the same nature such as the fire incident in the modular COVID-19 hospital in Tetovo that caused 14 deaths and the „Besa Trans“ bus fire incident in Bulgaria that caused 45 deaths.  
* Citizen movements in North Macedonia have gathered support in the

* countries in the region ,including Serbia, Greece, and Slovenia but also throughout the Macedonian diaspora in Europe and the rest of the world.

* There have been numerous instances of politically motivated hate speech and spread of misinformation, allegedly caused by different political actors with a goal of discrediting the citizen movement as not being legitimate nor independent from any political influence.

*Recognizing that:*

* Citizen protests are the cornerstone of every functioning liberal democracy

* The freedom of assembly and peaceful protest are fundamental rights that are protected under European and international law

* The actions of the Government of North Macedonia contradict fundamental European values and have been undermining its path of becoming a member of the European Union  
* A significant number of professional organizations, cultural institutions, athletes, and artists from North Macedonia and the wider region have supported the protests and marches.

*Therefore, LYMEC calls for:*

* Supporting the right of Macedonian people to protest peacefully, free from intimidation and political pressure

* The Government of North Macedonia to fulfill the demands of the protesters, including:
